title: Scramble Neutral
description: A transitional moment where neither player has clear control yet; the priorities are Head Position, hip control, Inside Position, and safety.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Scramble Neutral through Head Position, Inside Position, and directed pressure.
Win the head-and-hip race and move to a ride, pass, or Back Control.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Scramble Neutral with frames, Pummeling, or the right angle.
Avoid exposing the neck, back, or Knee Line while recovering base.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Head Position, hip connection, and inside hands.
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The Elbow-Knee Connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: If unsure, protect the neck, back, and legs, then reset your base.
Protect the neck, back, Knee Line, or arm line before countering.
If Inside Position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Win the head-hip race and settle the position
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
